I've started item 6 (b) with a read-only design packet to codex-proof2a (job `invoke-1790643930077-26991-210f2867`, park `park-8021e646`). I'm designing before building because a few choices determine every implementation step after it.

**What the design has to settle:**
- **Which status the scans are evidence about.** The scans measure the whole system, but the belief is kept per entity. The options are one declared entity (as in the first slice), a declared combination of all entities, or a hierarchical model.
- **A likelihood for each of the fourteen channels,** and what each scan producer must additionally save on the trace, as the first slice did for the support and attack counts.
- **Where the learned model plugs in.** The likely place is the status-belief update, where the hand-set prediction table would give way to a learned P(scan | status). Nothing in target choice reads status beliefs yet, so the design also has to say how the model would reach selection.
- **When a learned channel replaces its hand-set row.** This uses the same kind of BMR comparison as token A.
- **A circularity problem.** The before-scan beliefs used as labels were themselves produced by the hand-set model being replaced. The design needs the standard way to learn A together with the latent status.
- **The Lean declarations (b) needs.**
- **Whether ε belongs to (b) at all.** It sits on a different variable (the flight's token state), so it may belong elsewhere, or be classed by design for PROOF-2a.
- **A plan of 4–8 small implementation packets,** each marked if it needs a decision from you.

When it returns, I'll check its claims against the code and bring you the decisions with recommendations. I'll send the first packet straight away if it needs no decision from you.
